correctness.rationale: The proof reduces the common-neighbor problem to an exact extension lemma for codimension-one subspaces of binary nondegenerate spaces. The radical-zero and one-dimensional-radical cases both give exactly \(2^{n-k}\) LCD extensions. For an adjacent pair, every common neighbor is either a star extension of the intersection or a top subspace of the sum; orthogonal complementation counts the latter. The unique binary overlap candidate is degenerate in both radical cases, yielding \(\lambda=2^k+2^{n-k}-4\). Degree and triangle formulas then follow by exact double counting. A standalone exhaustive checker independently verifies every parameter \(2\le n\le6\).

value.rationale: The result resolves a directly identified structural problem for the binary LCD neighbor graph with an all-parameter closed formula. It strengthens a global triangle count to edge-regularity and supplies a compact proof using nondegenerate-space extension counts and the binary star/top decomposition. This is useful for local graph structure and potential clique/classification work, not a routine small-parameter census.
